issues.description: The problem statement requires the main function to indicate successful execution by returning 0 (problem_statement.md lines 21-22). In the reference solution (solution_repository/helloWorld.asm) the code explicitly sets eax to 1 before returning (mov eax, 1 at line 17), while the starter template (template_repository/helloWorld.asm) does not set eax at all before the ret (ret at line 18). This inconsistency means the solution does not adhere to the specified exit status and the template leaves the return value undefined, which can cause automated grading or execution checks to fail or behave unexpectedly.
issues.suggestedFix: Ensure main returns 0 to match the problem statement. In the solution change 'mov eax, 1' to 'mov eax, 0' (or insert 'mov eax, 0' immediately before ret). Also ensure the template example and any corrected starter code explicitly set eax to 0 before returning so the behavior is consistent and deterministic.

issues.description: The starter template uses a non-existent register name 'ecc' in the instruction 'add eax, ecc' (template_repository/helloWorld.asm line 13), while the problem statement explicitly instructs students to change 'ecc' to 'ecx' (problem_statement.md lines 15-18) and the reference solution uses the correct register 'ecx' in 'add eax, ecx' (solution_repository/helloWorld.asm line 12). This typo in the template prevents the code from assembling/compiling as-is and conflicts with the textual instructions.
issues.suggestedFix: Fix the typo in the starter template: replace 'ecc' with the correct register name 'ecx' so the instruction reads 'add eax, ecx'. This aligns the template with the problem statement instructions and the reference solution and allows the code to assemble successfully.
